commits.messageBody:
…config

Specify-phase artifact for #1698, which triage classified `T3` · `role:architect` ·
`hold:specify`. The spec is the gate here, so this records the design rather than
implementing it.

The sharper root cause than #1698's own wording. #1698 says validate.py is "fully managed
with no sanctioned extension point", which invites inventing one. Measured, the situation is
narrower and easier: `.minspec/config.json` ALREADY declares `specsDir: specs` and
`decisionsDir: docs/decisions`, and `.minspec/hooks/validate.py` never reads it - 0
occurrences of `config.json`, 0 of `import json`, 0 of `specsDir`, in the live file AND in
the `VALIDATE_PY` template. It hard-codes the same paths instead, at `:92` and `:105`. So the
extension point does not need inventing; it needs wiring to configuration the project already
has, which makes this a repair rather than a new feature surface.

Why it is invariant 2. A project extends the validator, a Refresh rewrites the managed region
from the template, the added corpus stops being validated - and the hook still exits 0,
because a validator that checks fewer files passes more often. Coverage shrinks silently.

Records two things the implementation must not do: no unmanaged region inside the managed
file (CQ-2, recommended against - a sanctioned edit point becomes a public contract that
cannot be withdrawn), and no silent fallback on a malformed config (FR-2 - that would
reintroduce the exact fault at the config-read step).

Three Clarify questions carry a recommendation AND its cost, per this repo's convention that
a recommendation with no stated cost is advocacy. CQ-1's recommended option is explicitly
noted as creating a second place the specs directory can be named, which is the same drift
class one level up.

`affects:` lists template-registry.ts rather than `implements:` - no spec claims that file
via implements:, and SPEC-066 and SPEC-063 both list it under affects: only.

`npm run validate` passes. It emits two expected warnings for this spec (missing design.md
and tasks.md, which T3 requires at Plan and Tasks) - correct for a Specify-only spec, and
deliberately NOT silenced with empty stubs, which is the anti-pattern #206 tracks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.messageBody:
…it's one-directional

Root cause: the spec's motivating example was written against commit e8dcaacb and never
re-measured before this PR opened; at head the claim that a refresh would "remove docs/domain
coverage" is false — the template already validates docs/domain, so nothing about it is lost.

Re-measured at ee8ea97c: .minspec/hooks/validate.py:92 validates specs + docs/domain; the
VALIDATE_PY template (template-registry.ts:1753-1757) validates specs + docs/decisions +
docs/domain, a strict superset (docs/decisions check confirmed via DR_ID_RE at :1681, absent
from the live file entirely). The real divergence is one-directional: a refresh would ADD
docs/decisions coverage and remove nothing.

Rewrote "The drift this repo currently carries proves the point" to state that measurement
plainly, with file:line citations, instead of the false bidirectional claim. Rewrote "Why
this is invariant 2, not a preference" so its illustration no longer depends on the specific
(now-false) direction: the property invariant 2 actually needs is that the hard-coded list
and config.json's specsDir/decisionsDir are never compared, so a FUTURE drift in either
direction would be just as invisible as today's benign one — not that today's drift already
proves the dangerous direction happened.

No FR, AC, or frontmatter changed; both edits are confined to the two Context subsections the
ai-review panel's reviewer and skeptic voters named (blocking finding on this PR).
